before.description: Records regulatory filings related to appeals including state and federal submissions and compliance reports.

Tracks billing disputes raised by employer groups or individual members contesting invoice amounts, payment applications, rate calculations, or retroactive adjustments. Captures dispute type (invoice amount, payment misapplication, rate error, retro adjustment, APTC discrepancy), disputed amount, dispute open date, dispute status (open, under review, resolved, escalated), resolution type (credit issued, invoice corrected, upheld), resolution date, and resolution notes. Distinct from clinical appeals managed in the appeal domain. [SSOT Master for dispute concept across domains]
Assignment of a care coordinator to a member or case.

Records formal contract compliance audits, post-payment reviews, and delegation oversight audits conducted against provider contracts and delegation agreements. Captures audit type (payment accuracy, credentialing compliance, delegation oversight, coding audit, medical record review, rate validation), audit period, audit scope, findings summary, overpayment or underpayment amount identified, corrective action plan (CAP), CAP due date, audit status (scheduled, in-progress, completed, findings-issued, CAP-pending), and next scheduled audit date. Supports NCQA delegation oversight standards, CMS program audit readiness, state DOI examination requirements, and SIU referral triggers.

Underwriting evaluation record and single source of truth for the complete risk assessment process from submission through rating through quote generation through decision for a new or renewing employer group. Tracks case submission date, group census data, prior carrier loss experience, medical underwriting status, risk tier assignment, manual rate basis; rating factors including age/gender composite factors, geographic area rating factors, industry risk factors, experience rating credibility weights, ACA-compliant rating adjustments, and actuarial basis documentation; underwriting decision (approved, declined, modified); and premium rate quotes with proposed rates by plan, coverage tier, and rating area, quote effective and expiration dates, rating methodology (community rated, experience rated, blended), proposed PMPM rates, total group premium estimate, and quote status (draft, presented, accepted, expired). Consolidates rating factors and rate quotes as stages within the underwriting case lifecycle. Links to the risk domain for RAF and HCC-based risk scoring at the group level. Supports the sales and renewal pipeline.
Master reference table for enrollment_batch. Referenced by enrollment_batch_id.

Transactional record of enrollment data submissions to CMS for Medicare Advantage, Part D, and Medicaid managed care programs via RAPS and EDPS. Captures submission batch ID, submission type (initial, correction, delete), CMS transaction ID, acceptance/rejection status, error detail codes, risk adjustment impact flag, and reconciliation status. Critical for government program compliance and RAF score accuracy. Sourced from CMS EDPS/RAPS response files.

Association entity representing the participation of a specific provider (NPI) within a specific provider network, capturing in-network status, effective and termination dates, tier assignment, accepting-new-patients flag, telehealth availability, panel status (open/closed), panel capacity, and credentialing linkage. This is the SSOT for the structural relationship between a provider and a network — distinct from provider identity (provider domain), contract terms (contract domain), and ACO-specific participation (aco_provider). Supports provider directory publication, CMS network adequacy filings, and member eligibility verification.

Transactional record tracking provider recruitment activities to address network adequacy gaps or strategic expansion. Captures target provider NPI/TIN, target specialty, target geographic area, recruitment reason (adequacy gap closure, strategic expansion, member request, competitor response), outreach date, outreach method, recruiter assigned, provider response, contracting referral date, and disposition (contracted, declined, no response). Links to adequacy assessment gap findings for remediation tracking. Supports network development pipeline management and regulatory gap closure evidence.

became.before: Records all communications related to appeal cases including notices, letters, and member/provider correspondence.
became.after: Records communication events and correspondence related to appeals, including notifications, letters, and member interactions throughout the appeal lifecycle.

became.before: Stores documents associated with appeal cases including clinical records, correspondence, and evidence.
became.after: Records documents submitted or generated during the appeal process, including supporting evidence, medical records, and decision letters.

became.before: Records grievances and appeals filed by members, providers, or other parties against health plan decisions.
Enrollment of a member into a care management program with status tracking and acuity assessment.

Audit and lifecycle tracking for all significant events in a contract's lifecycle — initiation, negotiation, execution, amendment, renewal, auto-renewal execution, suspension, termination, reinstatement, renegotiation, dispute filing, dispute resolution, and arbitration. Captures event type, event date, triggered-by user or system, prior status, new status, notes, approval chain. For renewal events: renewal type (auto, renegotiated, evergreen), rate change percentage, new effective date, and responsible contracting analyst. For dispute events: dispute type (rate dispute, scope-of-service dispute, payment dispute, termination dispute), disputed amount, dispute status (open, under review, resolved, escalated to arbitration), resolution outcome, resolution date, and provider relations case reference. SSOT for all contract state transitions, dispute management, renewal pipeline tracking, and provider relations workflows. Supports compliance audit trail, proactive contract management, and regulatory examination readiness. [SSOT Master for lifecycle_event concept across domains]
became.after: Contract lifecycle event with event_type_code constrained to contract events

became.before: Transactional record of a provider's signed attestation submitted as part of the credentialing or re-credentialing application. Captures attestation date, attestation type (initial application, re-credentialing, annual attestation), attestation questions answered (current competence, absence of impairment, no loss of privileges, no felony convictions, malpractice history accuracy, application accuracy), provider signature indicator, and any disclosures made. NCQA requires provider attestation within 180 days of credentialing decision. Each attestation submission is a distinct record. [SSOT Master for attestation concept across domains]

This association product represents the contractual relationship between an employer group and a vendor. It captures contract-specific details that exist only in the context of this relationship, linking one employer_group to one vendor per record.. Existence Justification: Employer groups negotiate separate contracts with multiple vendors, and each vendor can serve many employer groups. The contract itself carries attributes such as contract number, effective dates, status, total value, and review schedule, which are not owned by either the employer group or the vendor.
became.after: Employer contract details including terms, coverage, and agreement information
Eligibility Span entity for member domain

became.before: Operational record of formal member grievances (non-appeal complaints) filed against the health plan regarding service quality, access to care, provider behavior, billing disputes, or administrative issues. Tracks grievance receipt date, grievance type code (quality of care, access, attitude/service, billing/financial, benefit/coverage), issue category, member-reported description, assigned investigator, investigation timeline, resolution date, resolution type, resolution description, member satisfaction with resolution, regulatory reporting flag, and CMS/state DOI reportable indicator. Distinct from the appeal domain which handles coverage determination and claim denial disputes — grievances are expressions of dissatisfaction, not requests for coverage reversal. Supports CMS grievance reporting requirements for Medicare Advantage (42 CFR §422.564) and Medicaid managed care (42 CFR §438.402), state DOI complaint reporting, and NCQA accreditation standards (CR standards).

Core transactional record for each pharmacy claim submitted and adjudicated through the PBM system (RxClaim or Argus). Header captures: claim number, member ID, prescriber NPI, dispensing pharmacy NPI, NDC, days supply, quantity dispensed, fill date, adjudication date, claim status, reject codes, ingredient cost, dispensing fee, copay, coinsurance, deductible applied, plan paid amount, and coordination of benefits (COB) details. Line-level detail supports multi-ingredient compound claims and COB line splits: line sequence, per-ingredient NDC, ingredient cost, dispensing fee, sales tax, incentive amount, other payer amount, patient pay amount, and basis of cost determination. Supports NCPDP D.0 transaction standards, 835 remittance, CMS Part D encounter data submissions (EDPS/RAPS), 340B claim identification for duplicate discount prevention, and pharmacy audit trail requirements. This is the SSOT for all pharmacy claim header and line-level transactional data within the pharmacy domain.

Records mid-year or annual amendments to health plan benefit designs, cost-sharing rules, network configurations, service area modifications, or formulary changes. Each amendment captures the amendment type (benefit change, cost-share change, network change, service area change, formulary update), effective date, detailed description of change, regulatory approval status (pending, approved, denied), impacted benefit packages (as FK array), member notification requirement and notification date, CMS/DOI filing reference, amendment reason code, and whether the amendment triggers a new SBC document generation. Supports regulatory compliance with ACA mid-year change rules, member communication obligations under ERISA Section 104, and benefit configuration change management in Facets/QNXT.

Represents the contractual relationship between a health plan and a provider contract. Each record captures the effective and termination dates, current status, and the network context for the specific plan‑provider pairing.. Existence Justification: A health plan can be linked to many provider contracts, each representing an agreement with a specific provider. Conversely, a single provider can have contracts with multiple health plans. The relationship is managed as a distinct business entity that records effective dates, termination dates, status, and network context for each plan‑provider pairing.
became.after: Links health plans to provider contracts with participation agreements

became.before: This association captures the compliance relationship between a health plan and a regulatory obligation. It records the compliance status and key dates for each plan‑obligation pair, enabling the business to monitor and report on regulatory adherence.. Existence Justification: Each health plan must satisfy multiple regulatory obligations, and each regulatory obligation applies to many health plans. The compliance status, last assessment date, and next due date are tracked per plan‑obligation pair, forming a managed entity that business users maintain.
became.after: Tracks regulatory obligations and compliance requirements applicable to health plans

became.before: Represents the contractual participation of a healthcare facility in a provider network. Each record links one facility to one network and stores attributes that describe the nature of that participation.. Existence Justification: A healthcare facility can belong to multiple provider networks simultaneously, and each provider network includes many facilities. The relationship is actively managed (contracts/agreements) and carries attributes such as participation status and effective/termination dates.
became.after: Tracks provider participation in network arrangements, including effective dates, termination dates, and participation status.

became.before: Master record for all contracts and agreements executed between the health plan and third-party vendors — MSAs (Master Service Agreements), SOWs (Statements of Work), SaaS subscription agreements, maintenance agreements, and professional services contracts. Captures contract number, contract type, effective date, expiration date, auto-renewal flag, renewal notice period, total contract value (TCV), annual contract value (ACV), payment terms, governing law, contract status (draft, executed, expired, terminated), and the business owner responsible for the contract. Distinct from provider contracts (owned by the contract domain) — this entity covers non-clinical vendor relationships only.
became.after: Vendor-domain contract instance referencing vendor.vendor SSOT; distinct from contract.contract SSOT.

became.before: Transactional record for formal disputes raised against vendors — invoice disputes, service delivery disputes, SLA penalty disputes, and contract interpretation disagreements. Captures dispute type, dispute open date, disputed amount, dispute description, supporting evidence references, vendor response date, vendor position, internal resolution recommendation, dispute status (open, under negotiation, escalated, resolved, arbitration), resolution date, and final settlement amount. Supports accounts payable dispute management and contract enforcement workflows.
became.after: Vendor-domain dispute; references the contract.dispute SSOT via ssot_dispute_ref_id.

became.before: Repository and single source of truth for all documents associated with a vendor relationship — executed contracts, SOWs, BAAs, insurance certificates, W-9 forms, certifications, audit reports, RFP responses, NDAs, and correspondence. Captures document type, document title, document version, upload date, effective date, expiration date, document status (current, superseded, expired), storage location reference, and the business owner responsible for the document. Supports contract management, compliance audits, and vendor onboarding workflows.
became.after: Vendor-domain document subtype; document_type_code scoped to vendor documents.

became.before: Immutable audit trail of all significant lifecycle status transitions and events in the vendor master record — onboarding approval, tier reclassification, contract execution, suspension, reinstatement, termination, and offboarding. Captures event type, event timestamp, previous status, new status, triggering reason, event initiator, approving authority, and supporting notes. Provides a complete chronological history of the vendor relationship for compliance, audit, and governance purposes.
became.after: Vendor-domain lifecycle_event; event_type_code constrained to vendor events, distinct from contract/credential/member lifecycle_event.

became.before: Master record for professional certifications and licenses held by health plan employees — clinical certifications (RN, LCSW, CCM, CPC), compliance certifications (CHC, CHPC), IT certifications, and state insurance licenses. Captures certification type, issuing body, certification number, issue date, expiration date, renewal status, and verification date. Distinct from provider credentialing (which governs external clinical staff) — this tracks internal workforce credentials required for role eligibility and regulatory compliance. Supports NCQA care management staffing standards.

Percentage-based cost-sharing amount paid by the member for this pharmacy claim, calculated as a percentage of the allowed cost. Applies when the benefit design uses coinsurance rather than fixed copay. Contributes to OOP/MOOP accumulation.

Fixed dollar amount paid by the member at point of sale as their cost-sharing obligation for this pharmacy claim. Determined by formulary tier and benefit design. Contributes to member out-of-pocket (OOP) and maximum out-of-pocket (MOOP) accumulation.

Surrogate reference to the health plan member who is the beneficiary of this pharmacy claim. Links to the member master record in the Core Administration Platform (Facets/QNXT). Required for eligibility verification, coordination of benefits (COB), and CMS Part D risk adjustment (RAF/HCC).

Claim number of the original pharmacy claim that this record adjusts or reverses. Populated only for adjusted or reversed claims; null for original claims. Enables claim adjustment chain tracing for financial reconciliation, audit, and CMS Part D encounter data correction submissions.

Amount paid by another payer (secondary insurer, Medicare, Medicaid, manufacturer coupon) under coordination of benefits (COB). Used for COB reconciliation, 340B duplicate discount prevention, and CMS Part D TrOOP (True Out-of-Pocket) calculations.

Channel through which the drug was dispensed. Drives cost-sharing differentials, formulary tier rules, and network adequacy reporting. 'retail' = community pharmacy; 'mail_order' = 90-day mail service; 'specialty' = specialty pharmacy for high-cost/complex drugs; 'long_term_care' = SNF/LTC pharmacy; 'home_infusion' = infusion therapy at home.

Total amount paid by the health plan for this pharmacy claim after applying member cost-sharing (copay, coinsurance, deductible) and COB adjustments. Net total component of the MONETARY_TRIPLET. Used for 835 remittance, MLR reporting, and CMS Part D encounter data.

before.description: Records regulatory filings related to appeals including state and federal submissions and compliance reports.

Tracks billing disputes raised by employer groups or individual members contesting invoice amounts, payment applications, rate calculations, or retroactive adjustments. Captures dispute type (invoice amount, payment misapplication, rate error, retro adjustment, APTC discrepancy), disputed amount, dispute open date, dispute status (open, under review, resolved, escalated), resolution type (credit issued, invoice corrected, upheld), resolution date, and resolution notes. Distinct from clinical appeals managed in the appeal domain. [SSOT Master for dispute concept across domains]
Assignment of a care coordinator to a member or case.

Records formal contract compliance audits, post-payment reviews, and delegation oversight audits conducted against provider contracts and delegation agreements. Captures audit type (payment accuracy, credentialing compliance, delegation oversight, coding audit, medical record review, rate validation), audit period, audit scope, findings summary, overpayment or underpayment amount identified, corrective action plan (CAP), CAP due date, audit status (scheduled, in-progress, completed, findings-issued, CAP-pending), and next scheduled audit date. Supports NCQA delegation oversight standards, CMS program audit readiness, state DOI examination requirements, and SIU referral triggers.

Underwriting evaluation record and single source of truth for the complete risk assessment process from submission through rating through quote generation through decision for a new or renewing employer group. Tracks case submission date, group census data, prior carrier loss experience, medical underwriting status, risk tier assignment, manual rate basis; rating factors including age/gender composite factors, geographic area rating factors, industry risk factors, experience rating credibility weights, ACA-compliant rating adjustments, and actuarial basis documentation; underwriting decision (approved, declined, modified); and premium rate quotes with proposed rates by plan, coverage tier, and rating area, quote effective and expiration dates, rating methodology (community rated, experience rated, blended), proposed PMPM rates, total group premium estimate, and quote status (draft, presented, accepted, expired). Consolidates rating factors and rate quotes as stages within the underwriting case lifecycle. Links to the risk domain for RAF and HCC-based risk scoring at the group level. Supports the sales and renewal pipeline.
Master reference table for enrollment_batch. Referenced by enrollment_batch_id.

Transactional record of enrollment data submissions to CMS for Medicare Advantage, Part D, and Medicaid managed care programs via RAPS and EDPS. Captures submission batch ID, submission type (initial, correction, delete), CMS transaction ID, acceptance/rejection status, error detail codes, risk adjustment impact flag, and reconciliation status. Critical for government program compliance and RAF score accuracy. Sourced from CMS EDPS/RAPS response files.

Association entity representing the participation of a specific provider (NPI) within a specific provider network, capturing in-network status, effective and termination dates, tier assignment, accepting-new-patients flag, telehealth availability, panel status (open/closed), panel capacity, and credentialing linkage. This is the SSOT for the structural relationship between a provider and a network — distinct from provider identity (provider domain), contract terms (contract domain), and ACO-specific participation (aco_provider). Supports provider directory publication, CMS network adequacy filings, and member eligibility verification.

Transactional record tracking provider recruitment activities to address network adequacy gaps or strategic expansion. Captures target provider NPI/TIN, target specialty, target geographic area, recruitment reason (adequacy gap closure, strategic expansion, member request, competitor response), outreach date, outreach method, recruiter assigned, provider response, contracting referral date, and disposition (contracted, declined, no response). Links to adequacy assessment gap findings for remediation tracking. Supports network development pipeline management and regulatory gap closure evidence.

affected_objects.after: Records communication events and correspondence related to appeals, including notifications, letters, and member interactions throughout the appeal lifecycle.

affected_objects.before: Stores documents associated with appeal cases including clinical records, correspondence, and evidence.
affected_objects.after: Records documents submitted or generated during the appeal process, including supporting evidence, medical records, and decision letters.

affected_objects.before: Records grievances and appeals filed by members, providers, or other parties against health plan decisions.
Enrollment of a member into a care management program with status tracking and acuity assessment.

Audit and lifecycle tracking for all significant events in a contract's lifecycle — initiation, negotiation, execution, amendment, renewal, auto-renewal execution, suspension, termination, reinstatement, renegotiation, dispute filing, dispute resolution, and arbitration. Captures event type, event date, triggered-by user or system, prior status, new status, notes, approval chain. For renewal events: renewal type (auto, renegotiated, evergreen), rate change percentage, new effective date, and responsible contracting analyst. For dispute events: dispute type (rate dispute, scope-of-service dispute, payment dispute, termination dispute), disputed amount, dispute status (open, under review, resolved, escalated to arbitration), resolution outcome, resolution date, and provider relations case reference. SSOT for all contract state transitions, dispute management, renewal pipeline tracking, and provider relations workflows. Supports compliance audit trail, proactive contract management, and regulatory examination readiness. [SSOT Master for lifecycle_event concept across domains]
affected_objects.after: Contract lifecycle event with event_type_code constrained to contract events

affected_objects.before: Transactional record of a provider's signed attestation submitted as part of the credentialing or re-credentialing application. Captures attestation date, attestation type (initial application, re-credentialing, annual attestation), attestation questions answered (current competence, absence of impairment, no loss of privileges, no felony convictions, malpractice history accuracy, application accuracy), provider signature indicator, and any disclosures made. NCQA requires provider attestation within 180 days of credentialing decision. Each attestation submission is a distinct record. [SSOT Master for attestation concept across domains]

This association product represents the contractual relationship between an employer group and a vendor. It captures contract-specific details that exist only in the context of this relationship, linking one employer_group to one vendor per record.. Existence Justification: Employer groups negotiate separate contracts with multiple vendors, and each vendor can serve many employer groups. The contract itself carries attributes such as contract number, effective dates, status, total value, and review schedule, which are not owned by either the employer group or the vendor.
affected_objects.after: Employer contract details including terms, coverage, and agreement information
Eligibility Span entity for member domain

affected_objects.before: Operational record of formal member grievances (non-appeal complaints) filed against the health plan regarding service quality, access to care, provider behavior, billing disputes, or administrative issues. Tracks grievance receipt date, grievance type code (quality of care, access, attitude/service, billing/financial, benefit/coverage), issue category, member-reported description, assigned investigator, investigation timeline, resolution date, resolution type, resolution description, member satisfaction with resolution, regulatory reporting flag, and CMS/state DOI reportable indicator. Distinct from the appeal domain which handles coverage determination and claim denial disputes — grievances are expressions of dissatisfaction, not requests for coverage reversal. Supports CMS grievance reporting requirements for Medicare Advantage (42 CFR §422.564) and Medicaid managed care (42 CFR §438.402), state DOI complaint reporting, and NCQA accreditation standards (CR standards).

Core transactional record for each pharmacy claim submitted and adjudicated through the PBM system (RxClaim or Argus). Header captures: claim number, member ID, prescriber NPI, dispensing pharmacy NPI, NDC, days supply, quantity dispensed, fill date, adjudication date, claim status, reject codes, ingredient cost, dispensing fee, copay, coinsurance, deductible applied, plan paid amount, and coordination of benefits (COB) details. Line-level detail supports multi-ingredient compound claims and COB line splits: line sequence, per-ingredient NDC, ingredient cost, dispensing fee, sales tax, incentive amount, other payer amount, patient pay amount, and basis of cost determination. Supports NCPDP D.0 transaction standards, 835 remittance, CMS Part D encounter data submissions (EDPS/RAPS), 340B claim identification for duplicate discount prevention, and pharmacy audit trail requirements. This is the SSOT for all pharmacy claim header and line-level transactional data within the pharmacy domain.

Records mid-year or annual amendments to health plan benefit designs, cost-sharing rules, network configurations, service area modifications, or formulary changes. Each amendment captures the amendment type (benefit change, cost-share change, network change, service area change, formulary update), effective date, detailed description of change, regulatory approval status (pending, approved, denied), impacted benefit packages (as FK array), member notification requirement and notification date, CMS/DOI filing reference, amendment reason code, and whether the amendment triggers a new SBC document generation. Supports regulatory compliance with ACA mid-year change rules, member communication obligations under ERISA Section 104, and benefit configuration change management in Facets/QNXT.

Represents the contractual relationship between a health plan and a provider contract. Each record captures the effective and termination dates, current status, and the network context for the specific plan‑provider pairing.. Existence Justification: A health plan can be linked to many provider contracts, each representing an agreement with a specific provider. Conversely, a single provider can have contracts with multiple health plans. The relationship is managed as a distinct business entity that records effective dates, termination dates, status, and network context for each plan‑provider pairing.
affected_objects.after: Links health plans to provider contracts with participation agreements

affected_objects.before: This association captures the compliance relationship between a health plan and a regulatory obligation. It records the compliance status and key dates for each plan‑obligation pair, enabling the business to monitor and report on regulatory adherence.. Existence Justification: Each health plan must satisfy multiple regulatory obligations, and each regulatory obligation applies to many health plans. The compliance status, last assessment date, and next due date are tracked per plan‑obligation pair, forming a managed entity that business users maintain.
affected_objects.after: Tracks regulatory obligations and compliance requirements applicable to health plans

affected_objects.before: Represents the contractual participation of a healthcare facility in a provider network. Each record links one facility to one network and stores attributes that describe the nature of that participation.. Existence Justification: A healthcare facility can belong to multiple provider networks simultaneously, and each provider network includes many facilities. The relationship is actively managed (contracts/agreements) and carries attributes such as participation status and effective/termination dates.
affected_objects.after: Tracks provider participation in network arrangements, including effective dates, termination dates, and participation status.

affected_objects.before: Master record for all contracts and agreements executed between the health plan and third-party vendors — MSAs (Master Service Agreements), SOWs (Statements of Work), SaaS subscription agreements, maintenance agreements, and professional services contracts. Captures contract number, contract type, effective date, expiration date, auto-renewal flag, renewal notice period, total contract value (TCV), annual contract value (ACV), payment terms, governing law, contract status (draft, executed, expired, terminated), and the business owner responsible for the contract. Distinct from provider contracts (owned by the contract domain) — this entity covers non-clinical vendor relationships only.
affected_objects.after: Vendor-domain contract instance referencing vendor.vendor SSOT; distinct from contract.contract SSOT.

affected_objects.before: Transactional record for formal disputes raised against vendors — invoice disputes, service delivery disputes, SLA penalty disputes, and contract interpretation disagreements. Captures dispute type, dispute open date, disputed amount, dispute description, supporting evidence references, vendor response date, vendor position, internal resolution recommendation, dispute status (open, under negotiation, escalated, resolved, arbitration), resolution date, and final settlement amount. Supports accounts payable dispute management and contract enforcement workflows.
affected_objects.after: Vendor-domain dispute; references the contract.dispute SSOT via ssot_dispute_ref_id.

affected_objects.before: Repository and single source of truth for all documents associated with a vendor relationship — executed contracts, SOWs, BAAs, insurance certificates, W-9 forms, certifications, audit reports, RFP responses, NDAs, and correspondence. Captures document type, document title, document version, upload date, effective date, expiration date, document status (current, superseded, expired), storage location reference, and the business owner responsible for the document. after.description: Tracks billing disputes raised by employer groups or individual members contesting invoice amounts, payment applications, rate calculations, or retroactive adjustments. Captures dispute type (invoice amount, payment misapplication, rate error, retro adjustment, APTC discrepancy), disputed amount, dispute open date, dispute status (open, under review, resolved, escalated), resolution type (credit issued, invoice corrected, upheld), resolution date, and resolution notes. Distinct from clinical appeals managed in the appeal domain. [SSOT Master for dispute concept across domains]

Records formal contract compliance audits, post-payment reviews, and delegation oversight audits conducted against provider contracts and delegation agreements. Captures audit type (payment accuracy, credentialing compliance, delegation oversight, coding audit, medical record review, rate validation), audit period, audit scope, findings summary, overpayment or underpayment amount identified, corrective action plan (CAP), CAP due date, audit status (scheduled, in-progress, completed, findings-issued, CAP-pending), and next scheduled audit date. Supports NCQA delegation oversight standards, CMS program audit readiness, state DOI examination requirements, and SIU referral triggers.
Master reference table for enrollment_batch. Referenced by enrollment_batch_id.

Transactional record of enrollment data submissions to CMS for Medicare Advantage, Part D, and Medicaid managed care programs via RAPS and EDPS. Captures submission batch ID, submission type (initial, correction, delete), CMS transaction ID, acceptance/rejection status, error detail codes, risk adjustment impact flag, and reconciliation status. Critical for government program compliance and RAF score accuracy. Sourced from CMS EDPS/RAPS response files.

before.description: Tracks all formal amendments, addenda, and modifications to an existing provider contract. Captures amendment number, amendment type (rate change, term modification, LOB addition, network tier change), effective date, reason for amendment, negotiation outcome, approval status, and the specific contract sections modified. Maintains full amendment history for audit and compliance purposes. [SSOT Master for amendment concept across domains]

Association entity linking a provider contract to specific network configurations, defining which provider networks the contract covers. Captures network ID reference, participation tier (tier 1, tier 2, preferred, standard, narrow), in-network effective and termination dates, out-of-network flag, geographic service area, product line applicability (commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, exchange/QHP), and participation status (active, pending, terminated). Bridges the contract domain to the network domain for directory accuracy and claims adjudication network matching.

became.before: Accounts payable (AP) sub-ledger in Oracle Financials representing the full invoice-to-payment lifecycle for all financial payees — healthcare providers receiving capitation or fee-for-service payments, DME suppliers, TPA administrators, PBM partners, reinsurers, IT vendors, and professional service firms. Captures invoice attributes (invoice number, vendor/supplier ID, invoice date, due date, payment terms, amount, tax, currency, approval status, hold reason) and payment/disbursement attributes (payment method — check/EFT/wire, payment date, bank account, payment amount, void status, cleared date). Covers provider capitation payment runs, provider incentive settlements, VBC shared savings distributions, and routine vendor payments. Includes vendor/payee reference fields (vendor name, type, tax ID, NPI for provider-vendors, payment terms, 1099 flag). Feeds the GL upon validation and posting, and reconciles against bank statements. Single source of truth for the complete AP sub-ledger lifecycle from invoice receipt through disbursement and bank clearing.

Accounts payable invoice record submitted by a vendor for goods delivered or services rendered. Captures vendor invoice number, invoice date, invoice receipt date, invoice amount, tax amount, total amount due, currency, payment due date, payment terms, invoice status (received, under review, approved, disputed, paid, voided), PO reference, contract reference, and cost center allocation. Distinct from finance.ap_invoice which is the GL sub-ledger posting — this is the operational vendor invoice management record tracking the full invoice-to-approval workflow.

Records mid-year or annual amendments to health plan benefit designs, cost-sharing rules, network configurations, service area modifications, or formulary changes. Each amendment captures the amendment type (benefit change, cost-share change, network change, service area change, formulary update), effective date, detailed description of change, regulatory approval status (pending, approved, denied), impacted benefit packages (as FK array), member notification requirement and notification date, CMS/DOI filing reference, amendment reason code, and whether the amendment triggers a new SBC document generation. Represents the contractual relationship between a health plan and a provider contract. Each record captures the effective and termination dates, current status, and the network context for the specific plan‑provider pairing.. Existence Justification: A health plan can be linked to many provider contracts, each representing an agreement with a specific provider. Conversely, a single provider can have contracts with multiple health plans. The relationship is managed as a distinct business entity that records effective dates, termination dates, status, and network context for each plan‑provider pairing.

This association captures the compliance relationship between a health plan and a regulatory obligation. It records the compliance status and key dates for each plan‑obligation pair, enabling the business to monitor and report on regulatory adherence.. Existence Justification: Each health plan must satisfy multiple regulatory obligations, and each regulatory obligation applies to many health plans. The compliance status, last assessment date, and next due date are tracked per plan‑obligation pair, forming a managed entity that business users maintain.

Represents the contractual participation of a healthcare facility in a provider network. Each record links one facility to one network and stores attributes that describe the nature of that participation.. Existence Justification: A healthcare facility can belong to multiple provider networks simultaneously, and each provider network includes many facilities. The relationship is actively managed (contracts/agreements) and carries attributes such as participation status and effective/termination dates.

Audit and lifecycle tracking for all significant events in a contract's lifecycle — initiation, negotiation, execution, amendment, renewal, auto-renewal execution, suspension, termination, reinstatement, renegotiation, dispute filing, dispute resolution, and arbitration. Captures event type, event date, triggered-by user or system, prior status, new status, notes, approval chain. For renewal events: renewal type (auto, renegotiated, evergreen), rate change percentage, new effective date, and responsible contracting analyst. For dispute events: dispute type (rate dispute, scope-of-service dispute, payment dispute, termination dispute), disputed amount, dispute status (open, under review, resolved, escalated to arbitration), resolution outcome, resolution date, and provider relations case reference. SSOT for all contract state transitions, dispute management, renewal pipeline tracking, and provider relations workflows. Supports compliance audit trail, proactive contract management, and regulatory examination readiness. [SSOT Master for lifecycle_event concept across domains] [P204 skipped: target-product-missing:contract.contract_lifecycle_event renamed to contract.lifecycle_event per VREQ-006]

Association entity linking a provider contract to specific network configurations, defining which provider networks the contract covers. Captures network ID reference, participation tier (tier 1, tier 2, preferred, standard, narrow), in-network effective and termination dates, out-of-network flag, geographic service area, product line applicability (commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, exchange/QHP), and participation status (active, pending, terminated). Bridges the contract domain to the network domain for directory accuracy and claims adjudication network matching.

Transactional record of a provider's signed attestation submitted as part of the credentialing or re-credentialing application. Captures attestation date, attestation type (initial application, re-credentialing, annual attestation), attestation questions answered (current competence, absence of impairment, no loss of privileges, no felony convictions, malpractice history accuracy, application accuracy), provider signature indicator, and any disclosures made. NCQA requires provider attestation within 180 days of credentialing decision. Each attestation submission is a distinct record. [SSOT Master for attestation concept across domains]

This association product represents the contractual relationship between an employer group and a vendor. It captures contract-specific details that exist only in the context of this relationship, linking one employer_group to one vendor per record.. Existence Justification: Employer groups negotiate separate contracts with multiple vendors, and each vendor can serve many employer groups. The contract itself carries attributes such as contract number, effective dates, status, total value, and review schedule, which are not owned by either the employer group or the vendor.
HEALTH PLAN enrollment (distinct from care.enrollment care management program enrollment). Enrollment entity for member domain

Operational record of formal member grievances (non-appeal complaints) filed against the health plan regarding service quality, access to care, provider behavior, billing disputes, or administrative issues. Tracks grievance receipt date, grievance type code (quality of care, access, attitude/service, billing/financial, benefit/coverage), issue category, member-reported description, assigned investigator, investigation timeline, resolution date, resolution type, resolution description, member satisfaction with resolution, regulatory reporting flag, and CMS/state DOI reportable indicator. Distinct from the appeal domain which handles coverage determination and claim denial disputes — grievances are expressions of dissatisfaction, not requests for coverage reversal. Supports CMS grievance reporting requirements for Medicare Advantage (42 CFR §422.564) and Medicaid managed care (42 CFR §438.402), state DOI complaint reporting, and NCQA accreditation standards (CR standards).

Core transactional record for each pharmacy claim submitted and adjudicated through the PBM system (RxClaim or Argus). Header captures: claim number, member ID, prescriber NPI, dispensing pharmacy NPI, NDC, days supply, quantity dispensed, fill date, adjudication date, claim status, reject codes, ingredient cost, dispensing fee, copay, coinsurance, deductible applied, plan paid amount, and coordination of benefits (COB) details. Line-level detail supports multi-ingredient compound claims and COB line splits: line sequence, per-ingredient NDC, ingredient cost, dispensing fee, sales tax, incentive amount, other payer amount, patient pay amount, and basis of cost determination. Supports NCPDP D.0 transaction standards, 835 remittance, CMS Part D encounter data submissions (EDPS/RAPS), 340B claim identification for duplicate discount prevention, and pharmacy audit trail requirements. This is the SSOT for all pharmacy claim header and line-level transactional data within the pharmacy domain.

Master record for professional certifications and licenses held by health plan employees — clinical certifications (RN, LCSW, CCM, CPC), compliance certifications (CHC, CHPC), IT certifications, and state insurance licenses. Captures certification type, issuing body, certification number, issue date, expiration date, renewal status, and verification date. Distinct from provider credentialing (which governs external clinical staff) — this tracks internal workforce credentials required for role eligibility and regulatory compliance. Supports NCQA care management staffing standards.

Surrogate reference to the NDC-level drug master record in the pharmacy domain. Links to the formulary drug master product which carries NDC, drug name, tier, and pricing (AWP/WAC/MAC). Central to formulary compliance and drug utilization review (DUR).

NCPDP standard code indicating the outcome of the prospective drug utilization review (DUR) edit performed during adjudication (e.g., drug-drug interaction, duplicate therapy, dose check). Null if no DUR alert was triggered. Critical for pharmacy safety and regulatory compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product — NCPDP DUR outcome codes exceed 6 values]

The date the prescription was dispensed by the pharmacy to the member. This is the principal real-world business event date (BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category). Used for days supply calculations, refill-too-soon edits, and CMS Part D encounter data date of service reporting.

Formulary tier assigned to the dispensed drug at the time of adjudication. Determines member cost-sharing (copay/coinsurance) and plan benefit design. Tier 1 = preferred generic; Tier 2 = generic; Tier 3 = preferred brand; Tier 4 = non-preferred brand; Tier 5 = specialty; non_formulary = not on formulary.

Foreign key linking to claim.header. Business justification: Required for integrated care reporting: links pharmacy claims to the corresponding medical claim header for episode‑of‑care analysis and coordinated benefits calculations.

Surrogate reference to the health plan or benefit plan under which this pharmacy claim was adjudicated. Links to the plan and benefit product. Determines formulary, cost-sharing rules, and CMS Part D contract identification.

Surrogate reference to the health plan member who is the beneficiary of this pharmacy claim. Links to the member master record in the Core Administration Platform (Facets/QNXT). Required for eligibility verification, coordination of benefits (COB), and CMS Part D risk adjustment (RAF/HCC).

The cost of the drug ingredient(s) as billed by the dispensing pharmacy, before dispensing fee and other adjustments. Basis may be AWP, WAC, MAC, or negotiated rate. Core component of the MONETARY_TRIPLET for pharmacy claim financials. Used for PBM contract reconciliation and MLR calculation.

Indicates whether this pharmacy claim was dispensed under the 340B Drug Pricing Program (True = 340B claim). Used for 340B duplicate discount prevention, HRSA compliance reporting, and separation of 340B and non-340B claims in financial reconciliation.
Logical active flag for soft-delete and current-state filtering.

Indicates whether this claim is for a compounded drug product containing multiple ingredients (True = compound claim). Compound claims require line-level detail in the pharmacy_claim_line product. Used for compound drug utilization review and cost management.

Foreign key linking to finance.ledger. Business justification: Required for Claim Adjudication Posting process: each pharmacy claim expense must be posted to a GL ledger for financial reporting and regulatory audit.

Line of business under which this pharmacy claim was adjudicated. Drives regulatory reporting requirements, formulary rules, and cost-sharing structures. 'commercial' = employer-sponsored or individual; 'medicare_part_d' = CMS Medicare Part D; 'medicaid' = state Medicaid; 'exchange' = ACA marketplace QHP; 'cobra' = COBRA continuation coverage.
Cross-domain master/golden entity key for SSOT resolution.

Percentage-based cost-sharing amount paid by the member for this pharmacy claim, calculated as a percentage of the allowed cost. Applies when the benefit design uses coinsurance rather than fixed copay. Contributes to OOP/MOOP accumulation.

Fixed dollar amount paid by the member at point of sale as their cost-sharing obligation for this pharmacy claim. Determined by formulary tier and benefit design. Contributes to member out-of-pocket (OOP) and maximum out-of-pocket (MOOP) accumulation.

11-digit National Drug Code identifying the specific drug product dispensed, including labeler, product, and package segment. Denormalized from the drug master for claim-level auditability and CMS Part D encounter data submission (EDPS). Required for 340B duplicate discount prevention and drug utilization review (DUR).

Claim number of the original pharmacy claim that this record adjusts or reverses. Populated only for adjusted or reversed claims; null for original claims. Enables claim adjustment chain tracing for financial reconciliation, audit, and CMS Part D encounter data correction submissions.

Amount paid by another payer (secondary insurer, Medicare, Medicaid, manufacturer coupon) under coordination of benefits (COB). Used for COB reconciliation, 340B duplicate discount prevention, and CMS Part D TrOOP (True Out-of-Pocket) calculations.

Channel through which the drug was dispensed. Drives cost-sharing differentials, formulary tier rules, and network adequacy reporting. 'retail' = community pharmacy; 'mail_order' = 90-day mail service; 'specialty' = specialty pharmacy for high-cost/complex drugs; 'long_term_care' = SNF/LTC pharmacy; 'home_infusion' = infusion therapy at home.
Unique surrogate identifier for each pharmacy claim record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for the pharmacy_claim data product. Role: TRANSACTION_HEADER.

Total amount paid by the health plan for this pharmacy claim after applying member cost-sharing (copay, coinsurance, deductible) and COB adjustments. Net total component of the MONETARY_TRIPLET. Used for 835 remittance, MLR reporting, and CMS Part D encounter data.

10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the prescribing provider as submitted on the pharmacy claim. Denormalized for claim-level auditability, NCPDP D.0 compliance, and CMS Part D encounter data submission. Used for prescriber fraud/waste/abuse (FWA) analytics.

Date the prescription was written by the prescriber. Used to validate prescription age, enforce days-supply-from-written-date rules, and support medication adherence analytics. Distinct from fill_date (dispensing date).

Surrogate reference to the prior authorization record that approved dispensing of this drug, if applicable. Null when no PA was required. Links to the utilization management PA product. Required for specialty drug claims and step therapy override tracking.

Foreign key linking to contract.provider_contract. Business justification: Claim adjudication uses PBM contract rates, step‑therapy and rebate rules; linking claim to provider_contract enables accurate pricing and compliance reporting.

Surrogate reference to the prescribing provider who authored the prescription. Links to the provider master record in the Provider Management System (Cactus/ProviderSource). Used for prescriber profiling, fraud/waste/abuse (FWA) detection, and HEDIS measure attribution.

Actual quantity of the drug dispensed (e.g., number of tablets, milliliters, grams) as reported by the dispensing pharmacy. Used for quantity limit (QL) edits, drug utilization review (DUR), and CMS Part D encounter data submission.

NCPDP standard unit of measure code for the quantity dispensed. EA = each (tablets/capsules); ML = milliliters; GM = grams; UN = units; F2 = international units; ME = milliequivalents. Required for accurate quantity limit (QL) edit enforcement and CMS Part D encounter data.
